picks.headline: Blizzard Workers Secure Historic Contract Covering AI Use & Layoff Protections
picks.excerpt: Blizzard's 1,900-strong union ratified a contract that puts AI usage under negotiation with developers. It is the first major studio agreement giving creative staff a formal say in how generative tools enter their pipeline.
picks.rationale: First ratified AAA contract that makes AI adoption a bargaining item — sets the template every other studio's artists will now point at.

picks.headline: Genshin Impact dev HoYoverse wins $112,000 in court after AI company stole 63 of its characters' voices
picks.excerpt: A court awarded HoYoverse $112,000 after an AI firm cloned 63 Genshin Impact character voices with 'nearly identical characteristics.' The ruling is an early marker for how game voice IP is protected against synthetic reproduction.
picks.rationale: A real damages ruling on cloned character voices gives studios and VO talent the first concrete precedent to cite in contracts.

picks.headline: How ABCD Trains Large Gaussian Splat Scenes With Constant VRAM
picks.excerpt: Researcher Ka Heng Shiu details Alpha-Composited Block Coordinate Descent, which partitions huge radiance fields while keeping full-scene context during training. It lets artists train city-scale Gaussian splat environments without VRAM blowing up.
picks.rationale: The one pick that changes an environment artist's Tuesday — city-scale splat training stops being a VRAM lottery.

picks.headline: Acclaimed Visual Novel Studio Announces AI-Generated Quake Clone
picks.excerpt: Mages, the studio behind Steins;Gate, unveiled Juggernaut, a Quake-style shooter it admits was 'developed' almost entirely with AI. The reveal drew a near-unanimous negative reaction from English-speaking fans surprised at how far the generative pipeline went.
picks.rationale: A named, respected studio shipping an almost fully AI-built game is the clearest read yet on where the generative pipeline breaks in public.

picks.headline: TikTok Parent Reportedly Building AI Model to Rival Google's Genie for Real-Time Spatial Video
picks.excerpt: Bloomberg reports ByteDance is readying a world model for generating real-time spatial video, positioned against Google's Genie. The company hopes it becomes a 'flywheel' for immersive, generated interactive content.
picks.rationale: A second serious world-model player means generated interactive space stops being a Google demo and becomes a platform designers must plan for.
